question.problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =5\cdot 4+x\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (-3) \\  & =14-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 14-2x & =0 \\ 2x & =14 \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
